title: Pointers and memory in C
summary: Swap values through pointers, then diagnose a missing address in scanf.

scenario.briefing: A delivery queue needs an in-place swap, and a data-entry form silently writes to the wrong address. Repair both.

objectives.description: Apply the taught syntax in a working file.
Diagnose a realistic mistake and choose the correct repair.

hints: You need one temporary value to avoid overwriting the first value.
Finish by assigning the temporary to *right.

misconceptions.testDescription: The values are exchanged through dereferenced pointers.
misconceptions.feedback: Swapping the local pointer variables does not change the caller's integers. Dereference both pointers.

misconceptions.description: Passing an integer instead of its address to scanf.
misconceptions.feedback: The format is already %d. scanf needs the address: pass &count.

misconceptions.description: Thinking pointer assignment copies the pointed-to value.
misconceptions.feedback: Assigning one pointer to another changes which address is stored. Dereference to change the value.

sections.title: C functions and collections
sections.body: Functions declare return and parameter types: int add(int left, int right) { return left + right; }. C has no built-in dynamic array. You pass a pointer and a length, and you manage allocation explicitly.

sections.title: C errors and tools
sections.body: C functions report failure through return values such as NULL, -1, or an error code. errno carries details for some library calls. cc or gcc compiles, -Wall -Wextra enables warnings, make drives builds, and valgrind or sanitizers expose memory errors.

vocabulary.definition: Reading or writing the object a pointer points to.
A contiguous region of memory used to hold data.
An operation the C standard does not define, so any result is possible.

steps.title: Swap two values through pointers
steps.prompt: Edit main.c. swap receives two pointers and exchanges the values they point to.

tests.description: The swap function takes two integer pointers.
The values are exchanged through dereferenced pointers.

hints: Keep one temporary value so the first assignment is not lost.

localVerification.description: Compile main.c with warnings treated as errors using the C compiler.

steps.title: The form writes nowhere
steps.prompt: This program reads a number but leaves the variable unchanged. Select the faulty instruction and the correct repair.
steps.explanation: scanf needs the address of the object it should fill. Passing count by value gives it no writable location.
hints: scanf needs the address of the variable it should fill.
Passing count by value gives scanf no writable location.
The format %d is correct for int.

steps.title: Pointers and memory

statements.label: Writing *left = *right changes the value at the address left holds.
Assigning one pointer to another copies the pointed-to value.
The & operator produces the address of an object.
The swap function needs to free its parameters.

steps.explanation: Pointers hold addresses. Dereferencing writes through the address; assigning pointers only changes which address is stored.
hints: Assigning pointers changes addresses, not values.
